sovereign_country.strategic_role: 最高信誉财富保护、私人银行合规与楚格州加密谷Web3枢纽

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–People's Republic of China Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (1986, with 2009 Protocol)
Switzerland–China Double Taxation Agreement on Income and Capital (signed 25.06.2013; in force 2014)
Convention Establishing the European Free Trade Association (EFTA, 1960, as consolidated)
Switzerland–EU Bilateral Agreements I and II (trade facilitation, administrative cooperation, anti-fraud provisions)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing of 10 October 1997 (AMLA/GwG; SR 951.0), as revised by the Transparency Package of 22 December 2022; Swiss Code of Obligations (OR; SR 220) Arts. 927 et seq. (internal beneficial owner record for non-listed companies); Federal Ordinance of 15 November 2023 on the Central Register of Beneficial Owners (OR-UBO; SR 951.04); Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance of the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (AMLO-FINMA; SR 955.033.0); Embargo Act of 22 March 2002 (SR 946.231) and implementing SECO ordinances.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified identity/passport copies of each founder, director and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notarial or consular authority in the founder's jurisdiction of residency

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police Clearance / Certificate of No Criminal Record for each managing director residing outside Switzerland
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal record authority of the director's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if origin state is non-Hague)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter on the principal's account for source-of-funds verification (required by the notary and the AMLA obliged agent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank in the jurisdiction of the beneficial owner

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing the Swiss incorporation counsel, notary and domiciliation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal's local notary; authenticated by Apostille when executed abroad

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory multi-list screening for every natural-person shareholder, director, authorized signatory and UBO: (i) UN Consolidated Sanctions List and EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (ii) SECO sanctions measures under the Swiss Embargo Act of 22 March 2002; (iii) OFAC SDN and SSI lists for USD clearing and Swift correspondent-banking compliance; and (iv) PEP identification per Art. 2 lit. a AMLA and Arts. 20–21 AMLO-FINMA applying the 'prominent public function' test. Identified PEPs require enhanced due diligence: documented source of funds, senior management approval and monitoring for at least 12 months after termination of public function (Art. 12 AMLA). Screening is refreshed at each capital or ownership change and at least annually; for the Low_Risk_Standard B2B marketplace profile, completion occurs within 2–3 business days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (www.zefix.ch) operated by the Swiss Federal authorities; formal clearance granted and registration entered through the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of registered office (e.g., Zug, Zurich or Geneva).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Per Art. 950–951 OR and Arts. 26–29 of the Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV), the name must be written in Latin-script characters and may use German, French, Italian or Romansh, or a clear and non-misleading foreign-language transliteration into the Latin alphabet. Ideographic scripts (e.g., Chinese characters) are not registrable. The name must not violate the truthfulness principle (Art. 950 para 2 OR), must be capable of distinguishing the company from all prior-registered names at federal level, and must carry the statutory suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' (in the German canton of registration; 'SA' in French-language cantons).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banker, Sparkasse, Versicherung, Insurance, Trust, Fonds (require prior FINMA licensing or approval)
Swiss, Schweiz, Suisse, Svizzera, Eidgenossenschaft, Confederation, National, Federal (require authorization under the Federal Act on the Protection of Public Coats of Arms)
Holding, Group, Partner, Capital used in a way that falsely implies corporate-group status or financial strength (Art. 950 OR truthfulness rule)
Cryptovalue, Virtual Asset, Blockchain, Token or similar terms when combined with payment-rail activity, triggering enhanced FINMA substance and consumer-protection review
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Swiss federal law does not provide a stand-alone renewable name reservation; priority is established upon first filing of the incorporation application with the Cantonal Commercial Register. A cantonal pre-clearance letter is generally honoured for 30 days. On refusal, the registrar issues a written decision with reasons; the applicant may file an administrative appeal within 30 days of service with the cantonal supervisory authority (Handelsregisteraufsicht / Department of Justice), and a further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) under the Federal Administrative Procedure Act and ultimately to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court. Practical SOP: obtain written refusal; verify distinctiveness in Zefix; amend or substitute the conflicting or non-approved name elements; re-file the application with the corrected name; if the register persists in refusing an available name, escalate administratively as described.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted. The Commercial Register requires a verifiable physical address in the designated municipality and a functional service-of-process location. For ISIC 4791 (unlicensed B2B e-commerce), a licensed commercial domiciliation undertaking with physical reception, meeting facilities and available representatives during business hours is standard and accepted in Zug, Zurich and Geneva. A pure virtual mailbox without personnel or physical substance is rejected by the Handelsregisterämter and may trigger administrative sanction.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: estimated 5–10% per annum for a Low_Risk_Standard unlicensed B2B marketplace. Unannounced physical on-site inspections occur primarily upon suspicion of shell-company misuse, tax-substance desk audits, AML trigger events or abnormal payment-rail flows; use of a professional domiciliation office reduces inspection frequency materially.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Handelsregisteramt of the canton of registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff per HRegV and cantonal scale; CHF 500–1,200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official publication in Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) and Zefix index publication

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory gazette tariff per publication entry

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR / Code des obligations, CO; SR/R.S. 220), Articles 620–763 concerning the Aktiengesellschaft (stock corporation); supplemented by the Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV; SR 221.411), Article 936 OR on registration, and the Cantonal Notarization Act for the public deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), operating under the cantonal Department of Economic Affairs; final entries are published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation (Gründungsurkunde) executed before a certified Swiss notary, accompanied by the Registration Application to the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung), the escrow capital payment confirmation issued by a Swiss bank, and costs/registration fee statement.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum nominal share capital is CHF 100,000. At incorporation, at least 20% of the nominal value of each share must be paid up, being a minimum aggregate of CHF 50,000. The paid-in amount must be deposited and irrevocably blocked in an escrow account at a Swiss bank, evidenced by a bank certificate, unless alternative security is provided; capital in kind is permitted provided such contribution is fully disclosed, valued, and audited.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Incorporators approve and adopt the Articles of Incorporation of the Company as executed before the Cantonal Notary, and confirm the full subscription of the registered share capital of CHF 100,000, paid in escrow at a Swiss bank under Article 632 of the Swiss Code of Obligations. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office shall be at Baarerstrasse 10, CH-6300 Zug, Switzerland, and the Board shall manage escrow, filings, and bank account opening. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following officers are appointed effective immediately: [Name] – Chairman; [Name] – Member; [Name] – Secretary. RESOLVED, that the Chairman is authorized to execute the registration application and file it with the Commercial Register of the Canton of Zug.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name screening and escrow capital account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register name approval desk) and a licensed Swiss bank in Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name reservation application specifying legal form 'AG/SA'; verify the proposed name is distinctive, truthful, and does not conflict with existing registered names. Simultaneously open a blocked capital escrow account at the bank and deposit the minimum paid-up capital of CHF 50,000 (or the full CHF 100,000) in the name of the company-to-be. Obtain the bank's capital payment confirmation certificate for submission with the notarization.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Identification documents and passports of all incorporators/shareholders
Draft constitution/articles of association (pre-notary)
Bank account opening and AML/KYC questionnaire
Proof of legal capacity of corporate shareholders, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged, file revised name alternatives within 10 working days; an objection by a prior right-holder can be cured by obtaining a written consent or amending the name to include distinguishing elements; escalate to the cantonal register supervisory authority only if the rejection is unlawful.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial execution of the public deed of incorporation and election of corporate bodies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Certified public notary in Canton Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange an in-person or digital notarization session. The incorporators approve the final Articles of Incorporation before the notary, subscribe the shares, adopt the statutory governance provisions, elect the board of directors, and appoint the auditor unless an optional audit exemption applies. The notary verifies the bank escrow certificate of the paid-in capital and ensures compliance with Article 632 OR. The notary keeps the protocollized original deed and issues notarized certified copies for the registrar.
required_dossiers: Approved Articles of Incorporation/Charter
Bank escrow capital payment confirmation certificate
Passport or identity card of each incorporator and director
Declaration of residence and criminal record extract of directors (Swiss authorities)
Consent letters of directors, auditors, and authorized representatives
Notary engagement letter and fee schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the notary detect incomplete capital proof or a missing mandatory charter clause, the deed will be rescheduled without prejudice; deficiencies are cured by supplementary notarial declaration or revised capital certificate; any notarial fees already incurred are absorbed only if the notary caused the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of registration application to the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (central registry receiving application via ORZ/eGRIS electronic filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized incorporation deed and the signed registration application with the Zug Commercial Register, either electronically through the official register portal or in paper format. The application must state the company name, seat in Zug, purpose, paid-up capital, board composition and signatory powers (e.g., 'collectively by two' or 'individually'), and auditor details. The registrar examines statutory compliance, legal validity of signatures, and capital safeguards.
required_dossiers: Public deed of incorporation (original notarial protocol and extracts)
Signed official registration application form (Anmeldung)
Certified copies of notarized deed for each filing set
Bank certificate proving escrow of minimum paid-in capital
Board and auditor consent declarations
Name reservation confirmation from the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a deficiency or query notice, the applicant must cure the stated defects within the statutory curing period (usually 10–30 days); where the registrar refuses entry, the applicant may appeal to the Cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Commission and thereafter to the Cantonal Administrative Court of Zug within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SHAB publication, legal existence, and issuance of registry excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt – SHAB), operated by the Confederation; jointly initiated by the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon the registrar's final entry decision, the newly formed Aktiengesellschaft comes into legal existence. The Commercial Register notifies SHAB automatically, and the entry is published in the gazette. After publication, request an official registry excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug) which serves as legal proof of incorporation and company capacity.
required_dossiers: Commercial register application reference number
Notarized deed (already filed)
Payment receipt of registration fee (or debit authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains inaccurate corporate details, file a correction request with SHAB and the Commercial Register; legal third-party good-faith effects of publication are corrected by an amended entry; no prejudice arises for the company as the registration date is retroactive to the registrar's entry order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, VAT, and social security enrollments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Cantonal Tax Office Zug (Steueramt des Kantons Zug), AHV/SVA compensation office Zug, and SUVA (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for corporate income tax and capital tax with the Zug Cantonal Tax Office; register for customs/VAT with the Federal Tax Administration if annual taxable supplies exceed CHF 100,000 or where voluntary VAT registration is preferred for B2B marketplace operations. Enroll the company and employees with the AHV/IV/EO compensation fund, employer's BVG pension fund, and accident insurance with SUVA. File the registrar excerpt to evidence legal status.
required_dossiers: Commercial register excerpt of formation
Tax registration forms (Federal and Cantonal Zug)
VAT registration questionnaire and projected turnover
Shareholders and director identification documents
Employer registration forms (AHV and accident insurance)
Corporation bank account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration penalties are mitigated by filing voluntary disclosure with the competent tax office; any VAT registration refusal may be appealed to the Federal Administrative Court; delay in social security enrollment is cured by retroactive insurance clearing of premiums without criminal exposure where negligence is demonstrated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business premise, safety, and ancillary licensing clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Building Inspectorate of Zug, Zug Fire Brigade/Feuerwehr Zug, and Cantonal Civil Defense and Occupational Hygiene authorities (with SUVA coordination)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the building-use operating permit for the registered office and any physical warehouse or IT infrastructure premises under cantonal construction law. Schedule fire safety inspection, verify structural occupancy loads, secure evacuation and emergency lighting approvals, and submit the workplace occupational-safety self-assessment. A pure digital B2B marketplace requires no formal industrial manufacturing license, but the physical premises must pass inspectorate clearance prior to staff occupation.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement and floor plans of registered premises
Building permit or confirmation of exempt use
Fire safety prevention plan and equipment certificates
Structural occupancy / load inspection certificate
SUVA occupational safety checklist for office workplaces
OSHAS-compliant risk assessment report, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Negative inspection findings trigger a remediation order specifying a curing deadline; failure to comply can lead to suspension of the building-use permit; the company may file a remedial plan within 30 days and, against municipal orders, appeal to the Administrative Court of Canton Zug within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Economic Affairs of Canton Zug (Volkswirtschaftsdirektion) with Gewerbepolizei (trade police) supervision; no industrial license is imposed under the Federal Act on Trade and Industry (Gewerbegesetz) for a pure digital B2B cross-border wholesale platform.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempt – no statutory trade/manufacturing license applicable to electronic marketplace operations (Title of permit: Not applicable); standard commercial register entry and building operating permit for office premises suffice for legal operation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN, BAFU/UFAM) – Cantonal Environmental Directorate of Zug (Umweltschutzamt des Kantons Zug)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – digital B2B platform is a non-industrial information-technology activity without physical production; no EIA report or registration category applies, unless a separate warehouse/logistics facility creates emissions or traffic triggers a cantonal screening.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges are permitted. Office and server-room operations must comply with the Swiss Ordinance on Air Pollution Control (LRV/VoI), Annex 3 combustion emission limits, Ordinance on Chemical Risk Reduction (ORRChem/ChemRRV) for refrigerants, and Ordinance on Waste Movement; e-waste disposal and IT hardware recycling must follow the FOEN waste-management standards and the Ordinance on Recycling (VVEA).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification required from Feuerwehr Zug under the building permit, including smoke detection, evacuation route, and extinguishing equipment; structural load inspection of the registered office premises by the Municipal Building Inspectorate of Zug; occupational safety clearance obtained through the SUVA workplace inspection and annual risk assessment in accordance with Art. 82 of the Swiss Accident Insurance Act (UVG) and the Labour Act (ArG).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC), official portal www.estv.admin.ch; UID business identifier registry www.uid.ch; Swiss commercial register (Zefix) for company identification; for corporate income tax, the cantonal tax administration of the registered office (e.g., Zug, Zurich) remains the competent collection body, while ESTV administers federal income tax, VAT, withholding tax and stamp duties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: Assess VAT registration duty under Art. 10-14 MWSTG; a foreign entity without a Swiss seat is taxable from the first supply of goods or services performed in or into Switzerland, with no CHF 100,000 threshold exemption; voluntary registration is possible for a foreign business that purchases goods in Switzerland or has demonstrable taxable activity. STEP 2: Where the foreign entity has no Swiss permanent establishment, appointment of a Swiss tax representative or fiscal agent domiciled in Switzerland is mandatory (Art. 67(2) MWSTG); execute a written power of attorney and file it with the ESTV. STEP 3: File the electronic VAT registration application through the ESTV e-service portal (form 23 / registration for VAT), attaching: home-country commercial register extract or certificate of incorporation, Articles of Association / memorandum, passport or ID of legal representatives, board resolution authorizing the Swiss representative, and a brief description of the B2B marketplace business model and target counter-parties. STEP 4: ESTV verifies the file and issues the Swiss business identifier UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, e.g., CHE-123.456.789) with the suffix MWST, which simultaneously constitutes the VAT registration number; processing typically takes 5 to 20 working days. STEP 5: If the entity later creates a branch or permanent establishment in Switzerland, register the Swiss AG (Aktiengesellschaft) in the commercial register of the canton of domicile through a notary, obtain the UID via Zefix, and notify the cantonal tax administration for direct taxes; the VAT registration remains administered by the ESTV.

default_entity_tax_classification.territorial_scope: A Swiss-resident Aktiengesellschaft (AG) is subject to unlimited tax liability on worldwide income (federal, cantonal and communal corporate income taxes); a foreign-registered entity operating a Swiss B2B marketplace without a Swiss seat is subject only to limited/subject-to-tax nexus for income attributable to a Swiss permanent establishment, Swiss real estate, or Swiss-source claims; the AG is not a pass-through entity. Foreign shareholders of a Swiss AG are not taxed in Switzerland on dividends except for federal withholding tax of 35%, reduced under applicable double tax treaties.
default_entity_tax_classification.note: Switzerland has no general tax-exempt free zones. Ring-fenced benefits exist at cantonal level: patent/IP box, additional research and development super-deduction, notional interest deduction (NID) on qualifying excess equity, and cantonal tax holidays for newly established business operations in certain cantons (e.g., Geneva, Ticino, Zug); all are elective incentives, not full territorial exclusions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide a check-the-box entity classification; a Swiss AG is mandatorily taxed as an independent corporate entity. Available statutory elections relevant to the B2B marketplace: (1) VAT group election (Art. 21 MWSTG) allowing closely linked entities to be one VAT taxpayer with a single UID; (2) cash-basis VAT accounting method (Istmethode, taxation on received consideration) electable for turnover up to CHF 5 million; otherwise the accrual method (Sollmethode) applies mandatorily; (3) voluntary VAT registration for businesses below the CHF 100,000 threshold; (4) small-business VAT exemption election (Art. 11 MWSTG) with forfeiture of input VAT recovery; (5) customs simplifications (local clearance, AEO, e-dec export authorization) which are procedural elections; (6) tax incentive elections at cantonal level: patent box without separate expiry, NID, cantonal holding privilege status (for qualifying investment holdings). Hybrid mismatch: Switzerland ratified the OECD MLI on 26 August 2019 (in force 1 December 2019; effect 1 January 2020); no separate domestic hybrid or dual-consolidation election exists, but the MLI Principal Purpose Test and treaty override provisions neutralize hybrid arrangements; Swiss domestic law does not permit a partnership-style pass-through election for an AG.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA) governed by the Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009 (MWSTG, SR 641.20), as amended, administered by the ESTV.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of worldwide annual taxable turnover calculated on all supplies (excluding exempt supplies per Art. 10(2)(a) and Art. 21 MWSTG). A foreign supplier without seat in Switzerland is not entitled to the threshold and must register from the first taxable supply located in Switzerland, including distance sales of goods and electronically supplied services to non-business recipients; a foreign marketplace operator facilitating such supplies is deemed to be the supplier from 1 January 2025 under Art. 20a MWSTG and must register with the ESTV regardless of the freedom-of-trade threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime; there is no government-authorization API for invoice validation. Invoices must contain the statutory minimum content of Art. 26 MWSTG: full supplier name and address, UID plus MWST suffix, recipient name/address for supplies above CHF 400 or on request, date or period of supply, type, quantity and designation of the goods/services, consideration excluding tax, and applicable VAT rate; QR-invoices (Swiss QR-Code with QR-IBAN) are mandatory from 30 June 2020 for payment slips and serve as the standardized e-invoice payment trigger. For B2B electronic invoicing, Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 is the recommended national exchange standard; federal administration procurement (B2G) is migrating to mandatory Peppol-based e-invoicing; ESTV may request electronic delivery of VAT returns via its e-service (SwissTax/Inward e-services). No real-time clearance requirement applies to the marketplace platform, but from 1 January 2025 platforms deemed suppliers (Art. 20a MWSTG) must submit periodic electronic reporting and maintain transactional records usable by the ESTV upon demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods by a Swiss-registered business is zero-rated under Art. 23(1) MWSTG where the goods are physically transported abroad as part of a taxable supply and the export is evidenced by customs documentation; the 0% rate also covers direct costs ancillary to the export (transport, loading, commission for the export transaction). Exported B2B marketplace platform services (digital intermediation, listing, commission charges) provided to recipients whose economic seat is abroad fall outside the Swiss place-of-supply under Art. 18(1)(a) MWSTG and are outside the scope of Swiss VAT rather than technically zero-rated; no VAT is chargeable on such invoices and no Swiss input VAT deduction is associated with them. For physical goods sold by the Swiss AG through its B2B platform to foreign buyers, the zero-rating condition requires that title to the goods transfers abroad and that the Swiss exporter keeps verifiable proof of departure, membership of the customs-export documentation, and bank evidence of payment received from the non-resident counter-party; Swiss VAT law prescribes no specific statutory deadline for the receipt of foreign currency, but after the 180-day benchmark without inward remittance the ESTV will treat the export proof as incomplete unless documented exceptional terms exist.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration filed in the Swiss customs IT systems (e-dec, Passar / CRC / NCTS) with the printed export acknowledgment and, where applicable, the customs seal of the border office (Ausfuhrabfertigung)
Transport document evidencing physical dispatch from Swiss territory: ocean Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB), CMR international road consignment note, or CIM rail consignment note
Commercial export invoice including Incoterms, customs value, quantity, full goods description, HS codes, and exporter UID-MWST number
Inward remittance certificate or bank credit confirmation (SWIFT MT103 or account statement) naming the Swiss export entity as beneficiary for the invoiced value
Customs export confirmation (Ausfuhrbescheinigung) issued by Swiss customs and, if applicable, EUR.1 / ATR movement certificates for preferential trade arrangements
Packing list and freight booking evidence (recommended supplementary documents to reconcile quantities and support the customs declaration)
Marketplace order records and platform-generated contract documentation establishing the B2B relationship, buyer identity, and payment settlement chain
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV scrutinizes export zero-rating claims by cross-matching the customs export declaration, transport document, invoice sequence, platform contract data and banking remittances; if any mandatory document is missing, invalid, or inconsistent, the supply is re-characterized as a domestic taxable supply and Swiss VAT of 8.1% (or the applicable reduced rate) is retroactively assessed on the full invoice amount, together with default interest at the statutory rate of 4.5% per annum (2024). Tax evasion under Art. 58 MWSTG attracts a fine of up to three times the tax evaded; qualified VAT fraud under Art. 59 MWSTG is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years and/or a fine, and the prison penalty can be combined. The statutory limitation periods for retrospective assessment are 5 years for ordinary cases and 10 years for fraud or willful evasion; clawback applies to all supplies for which the exporter cannot produce the required export proof within the assessment period. In addition, the taxpayer must retain all books, vouchers, customs declarations, B/L, AWB/CMR and payment certificates for 10 years (Art. 42 MWSTG); a refund of input VAT claimed in connection with an invalid export is treated as a false credit and may be recovered with interest, plus penal sanctions. Estonian-style or non-substantive export window dressing, round-tripping of goods via bonded warehouses, and delayed or missing FX repatriation beyond the 180-day benchmark without documented commercial justification are red flags that trigger extended audit depth and possible criminal referral.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) — Schweizerische Nationalbank, together with the Federal Department of Finance (FDF) and the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) for banking conduct and money-laundering oversight. Exchange control policy is anchored in the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (CPIA) and the Federal Act on Economic Measures (EMG), which codifies Switzerland's long-standing liberal foreign-exchange regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CHF is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Switzerland imposes no exchange controls, no limitations on profit repatriation, and no prior central-bank approval for cross-border wire transfers, foreign-currency accounts, or investments by non-residents. Dividends and liquidation proceeds of an AG are freely remittable to foreign shareholders, subject to a 35% federal withholding tax, reducible under the relevant double-taxation treaty (DTT), including the Swiss–China DTT (2013) for Chinese shareholders. No restrictions apply to the holding of CNY, USD, or EUR accounts by Swiss-resident treasury entities. No SNB reporting is required except statistical balance-of-payments filings for external assets/liabilities above CHF 10M.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender rule exists under Swiss law. Exporters and cross-border platform operators may retain the full amount of export proceeds in any currency indefinitely, with no mandatory conversion timeline or ratio. Receipts from B2B platform sales may be kept separately in foreign currency for hedging or reinvestment purposes without any requirement to repatriate or convert into CHF.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Multi-Currency Settlement Account (CHF, USD, EUR, CNY)
Capital Escrow Account / Platform Collections Account
E-Commerce Operational Account / SEPA Direct Debit Rail

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Suisse AG (integrated into UBS Switzerland AG)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Historical entity — no separate new onboarding; legacy accounts migrated to UBS

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low feasibility. A FINMA-licensed Swiss fintech company under Art. 1b Banking Act or a licensed payment institution may offer corporate e-money accounts and access to the Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) system; however, offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK, Lithuania, Singapore EMI licensees) without a FINMA branch or Swiss partnership cannot hold CHF IBANs, cannot obtain direct SIC membership, and are prohibited from performing payment services for Swiss-resident entities under Art. 4 of the Banking Act. For Alibaba Pay settlement receipts, a Swiss-licensed EMI with a bank partner may receive CNY/USD flows, but legal certainty and prudential safeguarding are materially stronger with a Tier-1 bank relationship. A direct FINMA banking license is not required for the B2B marketplace itself because ordinary wholesale platform operation is not a regulated financial activity, but any treasury function holding client funds would trigger either a banking license or fintech-license perimeter.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is de facto mandatory for new corporate clients. Under Art. 9 AMLO-FINMA and FINMA Circular 2016/07, the mandatory face-to-face identification of natural persons (directors and beneficial owners) must be completed by a member of the group executive board, a signatory, or the UBO. Remote video identification is only accepted if performed via a FINMA-accredited electronic identification provider and even then the majority of Swiss Tier-1 banks will require an in-person meeting at a Swiss branch for an AG holding a treasury escrow mandate. A pragmatic pathway: notarized passport copies at a Swiss embassy or consulate, plus a physical bank visit by at least one executive director. If no physical attendance is possible, onboarding viability drops to Medium/Low, except for PostFinance which offers a fully digital client portal but still requires verification of directors' identity through certified electronic ID or a Swiss notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: B2B marketplace receiving payments from non-EU/EFTA counterparties (including Chinese suppliers via Alibaba Trade Assurance) at high frequency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Handelsregisterauszug (Commercial Register extract), articles of association, definitive transaction flow diagram, list of top 10 counterparties with LEI or Chinese business licenses, audited financial statements for two years, VAT registration certificate, customs declarations (EMED), plus a written statement of the marketplace's refund and escrow logic.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection from a non-Swiss shareholder to fund escrow reserves
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized capital increase deed, shareholders' register extract, board resolution fixing the contribution amount, source-of-funds documentation (bank statements, prior sale contract, dividend distribution minutes), Swiss stamp duty clearance certificate for paid-in capital above CHF 1M, and tax clearance certificate from the Cantonal Tax Office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of Alipay Global / Alibaba.com cross-border settlement rails with CNY-denominated receipts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alibaba.com marketplace membership certificate, Trade Assurance contract, Alipay Global merchant agreement, KYC file of the Chinese beneficiary, form of payment settlement schedule, and a Swiss legal opinion confirming that no banking activity is triggered by facilitating supplier payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Minimal operational substance (virtual office, no local employees, managed address)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office lease of at least 12 months, mandatory UID (Swiss unified business identification) number, AHV/AVS social-insurance registration of at least one Swiss-resident employee, appointment of a Swiss resident director, and appointment of a licensed Swiss audit firm for the statutory audit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between declared business (retail-like marketplace) and high-value B2B invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standardized international purchase orders, proforma invoices and final invoices matching the ISIC 4791 / NAICS 425120 classification, warehousing or logistics service agreements, and a documentary trail of merchant onboarding due diligence performed by the platform.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injection should be routed via SWIFT MT103 (single-customer credit transfer) or MT202 COV for interbank cover payments where the beneficiary is a Swiss bank. For CHF funding the wire should settle over SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) in real time; for foreign currency (USD/EUR/CNY), the credit must be processed via the correspondent bank of the Swiss clearing institution (e.g., UBS New York, ZKB Frankfurt, or Bank of China Zurich for CNY). The transaction narrative must reference the Commercial Register filing number and notarial deed; the SNB payment-statistics purpose code 'S62' (capital transfers) is required for equity injections, while 'S30' (foreign trade in goods) is required for operational trade remittances. Verification procedures: funds must be booked to a dedicated capital reserve account, the CHF 100M threshold triggering stamp duty must be checked, and the SNB external-assets reporting must be filed monthly when the receivable from non-residents exceeds CHF 10M.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier wires, using the beneficiary's IBAN and BIC with purpose code 'S30' for goods and 'S31' for services; (ii) irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit issued under UCP 600 via SWIFT MT700/MT707 for large consignments from Chinese manufacturers; (iii) SIC real-time gross settlement for domestic CHF disbursements to Swiss warehouses or fulfilment providers; (iv) SEPA Instant/SEPA Credit Transfer for suppliers within the EU/EEA; (v) Alibaba Pay Trade Assurance settlement with funds released through Alipay Global's escrow chain to the Chinese supplier's CNY or USD account. For USD disbursements, CHIPS or Fedwire via the bank's U.S. correspondent is the standard. Liquidity should be structured as: a master operational account (CHF), a foreign-currency sub-ledger (EUR/USD/CNY), and a segregated escrow ledger for marketplace pass-through funds to avoid commingling risk in the event of platform insolvency.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (deliverable) on CHF/USD, CHF/EUR, and CHF/CNH with tenors up to 12 months, executed under a standard ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or Swiss Master Agreement for OTC derivatives with the clearing bank

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the CNH/USD and onshore CNY/USD rates, offered by FINMA-licensed counterparties in Zurich and Geneva, requiring provisional margin collateral under an ISDA CSA

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between CHF and USD or CNY for both principal and coupon exchange, settled via continuous linked settlement (CLS) to mitigate settlement risk, counterparty limited to Tier-1 banks
European-style FX options (EUR/CHF, CNY/CHF) with upfront premium in CHF, permissible for hedged trade flows but not for speculative positions under corporate mandate rules

FX swaps (spot vs. forward) for short-term liquidity re-profiling where the marketplace receives USD and must fund EUR supplier obligations without touching the CHF treasury base, cleared via SIX x-clear or bilaterally with CLS settlement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate tax return package for federal, cantonal and communal income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) and competent Cantonal Tax Authority (e.g., Zug / Zurich tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end; for 31 December balance sheet date, commonly due by 30 June (extension of up to three months may be granted)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on unpaid tax at 4.5%–5% per annum; late filing penalty up to CHF 20,000; estimated assessment may be issued; persistent non-filing can lead to compulsory liquidation and removal from the Commercial Register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (if the taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 and the annual reporting period is selected)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) – VAT Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annual VAT reporting: 30 June of the following year; for quarterly reporting: within 45 days after quarter-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 4.5% per annum; administrative fine up to CHF 1,000 per missing declaration; estimated VAT assessment by the tax authority; repeated violations may be treated as tax evasion with criminal penalty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audit report and financial statements presented to the shareholders' general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the Aktiengesellschaft; no external government filing when audit is not mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance sheet date; the AGM must be held within this period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director and board liability for late convocation; administrative criminal proceeding for infringement of corporate law; inability to validly discharge management and approve accounts without an audit report where audit is required

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit is mandatory if two of the three following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: total balance sheet above CHF 20 million; total turnover above CHF 40 million; average full-time employees above 250. A limited (review) audit may be performed below those thresholds. Small companies may waive an audit if they do not reach two of three smaller thresholds (procedural 'opting-out').
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957 et seq.) and Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS permitted for listed companies; FINMA regulations apply if licensed as financial intermediary

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act, a corporate entity is not required to file an annual UBO statement to a national registry; however, the company must maintain an up-to-date and complete register of beneficial owners within the company records. This internal register must be reviewed at least annually by the board, corrected upon any shareholding transfer, and shown to the statutory auditor or authorized government authorities upon request. Auditors, if appointed, will verify the existence and correctness of the UBO register during the annual audit procedure.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholder ledger with ultimate beneficial owners) in accordance with Art. 686 CO
Minute Book of General Meetings and Board of Directors Meetings
Business books and annual financial statements archive (10-year retention)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $300 – $2,000 per annum (registered seat, mail forwarding, commercial agent services unless performed by management)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,000 – $8,000 for a limited audit review; $10,000 – $30,000 for an ordinary audit of a small to medium-size B2B marketplace platform

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% (federal) – combined effective rate varies by canton, typically 12-15%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent box regime, R&D super deduction, notional interest deduction (in some cantons), participation exemption for substantial shareholdings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal and cantonal corporate tax return (Formulaire pour personnes morales) filed via the e-System (e.g., eTax for legal entities) or paper; integrated federal/cantonal filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; for calendar year-end, typically by 30 June of the following year (extensions possible).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax (per commercial accounts)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Swiss-source income only; allocate expenses accordingly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses (e.g., taxes, excessive director fees)
Deductions for participation exemption and patent box relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only if applicable to Swiss-source income.
Ensure correct allocation of income and expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax calculation (8.5% on taxable income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply federal rate; cantonal/communal rates vary.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: CHF 100–1,000 per month (up to CHF 10,000); late payment interest; criminal fines up to 3x tax evaded for deliberate evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% (statutory), reduced under tax treaties (e.g., 0-15% for qualifying shareholders).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the beneficial owner must submit Form 823 (for dividends) or Form 824 (for interest) to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) along with a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority. The FTA processes refunds or grants exemption at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% statutory withholding tax (no WHT on royalties). Interest: 35% statutory on bond interest, but 0% on bank interest and most commercial interest; treaty rates may reduce.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if related-party transactions exceed CHF 1 million (goods) or CHF 500,000 (services) per year; Master File required if group turnover exceeds CHF 1 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not have specific ESR, but requires economic substance for tax residency and to avoid treaty abuse; companies must have actual substance (office, staff, decision-making) to benefit from tax treaties and participation exemption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful misrepresentation of income or expenses, false documentation, or concealment of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 3 times the tax evaded, plus interest; criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participate in evasion; travel bans and imprisonment up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without economic substance solely to obtain tax benefits or treaty advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of taxable income, penalties up to 100% of tax due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties and criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with anti-money laundering obligations in B2B transactions (e.g., inadequate KYC, suspicious transaction reporting).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CHF 500,000, revocation of license, criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for AML breaches, including imprisonment up to 5 years.
